Nguyen Hue was born in the year of Quy Dau 1753, the 13th year of the Canh Hung reign under King Le Hien Tong of the Later Le Dynasty. He was also known as Quang Binh,[11] Van Hue[12], or Ho Thom. The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. 3,	"Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Nguyen Hue was born in the year of Quy Dau 1753, the 13th year of the Canh Hung reign under King Le Hien Tong of the Later Le Dynasty. He was also known as Quang Binh,[11] Van Hue[12], or Ho Thom. Later, local people often called him Duc Ong Binh (Lord Binh)[13] or Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight).[8] According to Quang Trung anh hùng dân tộc (Quang Trung the National Hero), "Nguyen Hue had curly hair, textured skin, eyes that flashed like lightning, a voice as resonant as a bell, agile, strong, and brave." The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. Nguyen Lu was called Duc Ong Bay (Lord Seven) and Nguyen Hue was Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight); Le Trong Ham in the book Minh đô sử argued that Ho Phi Phuc fathered "Nhac, Lu, then two daughters, and then Hue".

Growing up, he, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were sent to study both literature and martial arts with teacher Truong Van Hien. Truong Van Hien was a retainer of Truong Van Hanh, and Truong Van Hanh was the teacher of Nguyen Phuc Luan – Nguyen Anh's father. After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh. It was this teacher who discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel to build a great enterprise. Legend has it that the prophecy "Tay khoi nghia, Bac thu cong" (Rebel in the West, achieve success in the North) originated from Truong Van Hien.[14] Legend also has it that Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were all highly skilled in martial arts and were the founders of several Binh Dinh martial arts styles. Nguyen Hue created Yen Phi Quyen (Swallow Flight Form), Nguyen Lu created Hung Ke Quyen (Rooster Form), and all three Tay Son brothers created Doc Lu Thuong (Single Censer Spear). The three Tay Son heroes played a huge role in the formation and development of the Tay Son Binh Dinh martial arts sect, being the leaders who created and reformed empty-handed and weapon forms to teach the army in the early stages of the uprising.[15]"
4,	"Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. During the reign of the 6th Hung King, in Phu Dong village, Vu Ninh region, there was a wealthy family who had a son. By the time he was over three years old, he ate well and grew big but did not know how to speak or laugh. At a time when there was urgent news of danger in the country, the king sent envoys to find someone who could repel the enemy. On that day, the child suddenly spoke, telling his mother to invite the royal envoy in, and said: "Please grant me a sword and a horse, the king needs not worry about anything." The king granted him a sword and a horse; the child immediately rode the horse, brandished the sword, and charged forward with the royal army following behind, defeating the enemy troops at the foot of Vu Ninh mountain. The enemy troops turned their spears against each other, with many casualties; the survivors all bowed down, revered the child as a heavenly general, and immediately surrendered. The child rode his horse [4a] into the sky and departed. The king ordered the child's home garden to be renovated into a temple for annual sacrifices. Later, Ly Thai To granted him the title Xung Thien Than Vuong. (The temple is located next to Kien So pagoda, Phu Dong village).

During the reign of King Cheng of Zhou [1063-1026 BC], our country of Viet visited the Zhou dynasty for the first time (it is unclear during which Hung King's reign), claiming to be the Viet Thuong clan, and offered a white pheasant. The Duke of Zhou said: "If our political decrees do not reach them, a gentleman does not treat them as his subjects," and then ordered the construction of a south-pointing chariot to escort the envoys back to their country.

At the end of the Hung Vuong era, the king had a daughter named Mi Nuong, who was remarkably beautiful. Thuc Vuong heard of her and came to propose marriage. The king wanted to agree, but the Hung Hau advised against it: "They want to conquer our country and are only using marriage as an excuse." Because of this, Thuc Vuong harbored resentment. The king, wanting to find a worthy person to marry her to, told his subjects: "This daughter is of fairy descent; only someone with sufficient talent and virtue can be my son-in-law." At that time, two men arrived from outside and bowed in the courtyard to propose. The king found it strange; when asked, they replied that one was [4b] Son Tinh (Mountain Spirit) and the other was Thuy Tinh (Water Spirit), both from the great realm, who had heard the king had a divine daughter and made bold to come request her hand. The king said: "I have only one daughter, how can I have both of you as worthy sons-in-law?" He then set a condition that the next day, whoever brought sufficient betrothal gifts first would marry her. The two men obeyed, bowed in gratitude, and left. The next day, Son Tinh brought jewels, gold, silver, mountain birds, and forest beasts as gifts. The king kept his promise and married his daughter to him. Son Tinh took his wife to live on a high peak of Tan Vien mountain. Thuy Tinh also arrived with betrothal gifts later; furious and regretful that he was too late, he summoned clouds and rain, raised the waters to flood the land, and led aquatic creatures in pursuit. The king and Son Tinh stretched iron nets across the upper reaches of the Tu Liem river to block them. Thuy Tinh took another river, from Ly Nhan to the foot of Quang Oai mountain, then followed the banks up to the Hat river estuary, out to the great river, and turned into the Da river to attack Tan Vien. Everywhere he went, he dug deep abysses and swamps, storing water to plot a surprise attack. Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. Kinh Duong Vuong
[1b] His taboo name was Loc Tuc, a descendant of the Than Nong clan.
Year of Nham Tuat, 17th year. In the past, De Minh, the third-generation descendant of Viem De of the Than Nong clan, fathered De Nghi. Later, during a tour of the South, De Minh reached Ngu Linh, married the daughter of Vu Tien, and fathered the king [Kinh Duong Vuong]. The king was a man of sagacious intelligence; De Minh loved him dearly and wanted him to succeed to the throne. The king persistently yielded to his older brother and dared not obey the command. De Minh then established De Nghi as the heir to rule the North, and enfeoffed the king as Kinh Duong Vuong to rule the South, calling it the kingdom of Xich Quy.
The king married the daughter of Dong Dinh Quan named Than Long, and fathered Lac Long Quan (Note: The Tang annals record: during the Kinh Duong period, there was a goat-herding woman who claimed to be the youngest daughter of Dong Dinh Quan; she married the second son of Kinh Xuyen but was abandoned, and wrote a letter asking Lieu Nghi to report this to Dong Dinh Quan. Thus, Kinh Xuyen and Dong Dinh had been allied by marriage for generations).

Lac Long Quan
[2a] His taboo name was Sung Lam, son of Kinh Duong Vuong.
The king married De Lai's daughter, Au Co, and fathered a hundred sons (legend has it she gave birth to a hundred eggs), who are the ancestors of the Bach Viet. One day, the king said to Au Co: "I am of the dragon race, you are of the fairy race; water and fire are incompatible, it is truly difficult for us to be together." They then bid each other farewell, dividing 50 children to follow their mother to the mountains, and 50 children to follow their father to the South (some versions record to the South Sea), and enfeoffed the eldest son as Hung Vuong to succeed the throne.
Historian Ngo Si Lien said: When heaven and earth were first formed, there was a being created from vital energy, which was the Pan Gu clan. From the manifestation of energy came the manifestation of physical forms; nothing exists outside the two energies of yin and yang. The I Ching says: "Heaven and earth intermingle, all things are transformed and purified; male and female unite their essences, all things are born." Therefore, there is husband and wife first, then father and son, and after father and son comes ruler and subject. [2b] However, the birth of sages and worthies is always extraordinary, which is due to the mandate of heaven. question: Who were the three brothers of the Tay Son movement?
answer:
The Tay Son movement, a significant historical event in Vietnamese history, was led by three brothers who played pivotal roles in the unification of Vietnam. These brothers were **Nguyen Nhac**, **Nguyen Lu**, and **Nguyen Hue**. Their leadership and military strategies were instrumental in the rise of the Tay Son dynasty, which briefly unified the northern and southern regions of Vietnam.

### Nguyen Nhac
Nguyen Nhac, the eldest of the three brothers, was known for his strategic acumen and leadership. He was often referred to as "Anh Hai Trau" (Brother Two Betel) due to his early trade in betel. Nguyen Nhac was instrumental in the early stages of the Tay Son movement, contributing to the planning and execution of military campaigns. His role was crucial in the initial rebellion against the ruling Nguyen dynasty, which was a significant factor in the eventual rise of the Tay Son brothers.

### Nguyen Lu
Nguyen Lu, the second brother, was known for his martial prowess and was often called "Thay Tu Lu" (Master Four Lu). He was a skilled warrior and played a key role in the military campaigns that led to the unification of Vietnam. Nguyen Lu's contributions to the Tay Son movement were significant, particularly in the battles against the northern dynasties. His leadership and bravery were celebrated in historical accounts, and he was also recognized for his role in the development of martial arts styles associated with the Tay Son movement.

### Nguyen Hue
Nguyen Hue, the youngest of the three brothers, was the most prominent and charismatic leader of the Tay Son movement. He was often referred to as "Duc Ong Tam" (Lord Eight) and was known for his strategic brilliance and military genius. Nguyen Hue's leadership was pivotal in the final stages of the Tay Son movement, leading to the defeat of the northern dynasties and the establishment of the Tay Son dynasty. His ability to unite the various factions and his military strategies were key to the success of the movement.

### Legacy and Influence
The three brothers of the Tay Son movement not only played a crucial role in the unification of Vietnam but also left a lasting legacy in Vietnamese history. Their contributions to the development of martial arts and their leadership in the face of adversity are still celebrated today. The Tay Son movement is remembered as a period of significant change and transformation in Vietnamese history, marked by the rise of these three brothers and their impact on the nation's political and cultural landscape.

The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. Nguyen Lu was called Duc Ong Bay (Lord Seven) and Nguyen Hue was Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight); Le Trong Ham in the book Minh đô sử argued that Ho Phi Phuc fathered "Nhac, Lu, then two daughters, and then Hue".

question: Summarize the main reforms of Quang Trung during his reign.
answer:
### Summary of Quang Trung's Main Reforms During His Reign

Nguyen Hue, also known as Quang Trung, was a pivotal figure in Vietnamese history, renowned for his military prowess and political reforms. His reign marked a significant period of consolidation and modernization within the Tay Son dynasty. Here is a summary of the main reforms he implemented:

#### 1. **Military Reforms**
Quang Trung placed a strong emphasis on military reform, recognizing the importance of a well-organized and disciplined army. He restructured the military to enhance its efficiency and effectiveness. This included the establishment of a centralized command structure and the integration of various martial arts styles, which were believed to contribute to the soldiers' combat skills. The reforms aimed to create a formidable military force capable of defending the kingdom and expanding its influence.

#### 2. **Administrative Reforms**
Quang Trung implemented administrative reforms to streamline governance and improve the efficiency of the state apparatus. He reorganized the bureaucracy to ensure that officials were competent and loyal to the state. These reforms included the establishment of new administrative regions and the appointment of capable administrators to oversee these areas. By centralizing power and improving the efficiency of governance, Quang Trung aimed to strengthen the state's ability to manage its vast territories.

#### 3. **Economic Reforms**
Economic reforms were a crucial aspect of Quang Trung's reign. He focused on revitalizing the economy by promoting agricultural production and trade. He encouraged the cultivation of staple crops and the development of infrastructure to support trade routes. These measures were intended to increase food security and economic stability, which in turn would support the military and the general populace.

#### 4. **Legal and Social Reforms**
Quang Trung introduced legal and social reforms to promote justice and social harmony. He worked to establish a more equitable legal system that addressed the grievances of the common people. These reforms included the reduction of corruption among officials and the promotion of social welfare initiatives. By addressing social inequalities and ensuring fair treatment, Quang Trung aimed to foster a sense of unity and loyalty among the populace.

#### 5. **Cultural and Educational Reforms**
Quang Trung recognized the importance of education and culture in the development of a strong nation. He supported the establishment of schools and the promotion of Confucian values, which were seen as essential for cultivating a well-educated and morally upright citizenry. These reforms aimed to create a more literate and informed society, which would contribute to the overall strength and stability of the state.

In summary, Quang Trung's reign was characterized by a series of comprehensive reforms that addressed various aspects of governance, military, economic, legal, and social life. These reforms were instrumental in consolidating his power and ensuring the stability and prosperity of the Tay Son dynasty.

Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

### Collaboration Between Skylar Grey and Alex da Kid

Skylar Grey's collaboration with Alex da Kid began in late 2009 when she was staying at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon. During this time, she was working on writing songs, and her experiences in an abusive relationship with the music industry inspired her creative process. She described this relationship as something that "beats me down," which influenced her writing. Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, seeking help in presenting her work. Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid, a British hip hop producer known for his work in the genre.

Alex da Kid sent Grey a track that suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships. As she listened to the track, she spontaneously began singing lyrics to the melody, which led to the creation of the chorus for "Love the Way You Lie." Grey recorded her vocals for Alex da Kid's demo, which included the track and its hook melody. This collaboration marked the beginning of the song's development.

### Introduction of "Love the Way You Lie" to Eminem

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered some backing tracks to Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales. Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was looking for a different musical approach for his next album. Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem requested more tracks and eventually heard "Love the Way You Lie." He was captivated by the song and decided to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna, whom he believed could bring the track to life.

Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off." His manager, Paul Rosenberg, sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted the collaboration at the last moment. Eminem then wrote the rapped verses to the song, completing the track and setting the stage for its eventual release as part of his seventh studio album, *Recovery*. This sequence of events highlights the collaborative efforts that led to the creation of "Love the Way You Lie" and its eventual selection by Eminem for his album.

The song **"Love the Way You Lie"** by Eminem and Rihanna is deeply intertwined with the personal experiences of both artists, particularly their struggles with abusive relationships. These experiences are reflected in the lyrics and the emotional tone of the track, which explores the complex dynamics of love and violence.

### Eminem's Experiences
Eminem's lyrics in the song reflect his past relationship with Kim Scott, his ex-wife. The song's verses contain references to emotional and physical abuse, which many interpret as a reflection of his real-life experiences. For instance, the line *"I laid hands on her. I'll never stoop so low again/ I guess I don't know my own strength"* is seen as a direct acknowledgment of his past actions toward Kim. Eminem had previously released songs such as **"Kim" (2000)** and **"'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998)**, which also depicted his fantasies of violence and abuse toward his then-wife. These songs, like **"Love the Way You Lie,"** suggest a pattern of emotional turmoil and a struggle to reconcile with past actions.

### Rihanna's Experiences
Rihanna's personal experiences with Chris Brown are also central to the song's theme. In 2009, Chris Brown was convicted of felony assault for beating Rihanna, an incident that received widespread media attention. The song's lyrics, particularly Rihanna's lines such as *"If she ever tries to fuckin' leave again, I'ma tie her to the bed and set this house on fire,"* are interpreted as a reference to this real-life event. Rihanna has publicly spoken about the impact of this relationship, describing it as a difficult and abusive chapter in her life. She has also mentioned that the song's theme of domestic violence resonates with her because she believes many people lack insight into the complexities of such relationships.

### Shared Experiences and Collaboration
Both Eminem and Rihanna have spoken about how their personal experiences with abuse influenced their collaboration on **"Love the Way You Lie."** Eminem described the song as one that "only she could pull off," recognizing Rihanna's ability to convey the emotional depth of the lyrics. Rihanna, in turn, felt a strong connection to the song's theme, stating that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" and provided a realistic portrayal of the issue. Their shared experiences with abusive relationships likely contributed to the authenticity and emotional weight of the song, making it a powerful commentary on the subject.

He wrote the rapped verses, which complemented Rihanna's melodic chorus, creating a dynamic interplay between the two artists. question: Arrange the main events in the song's development in chronological order.
answer:
# Chronological Development of the Tay Son Uprising and Quang Trung's Reign

## Early Origins and Family Background

The Tay Son uprising began with the rise of the Tay Son brothers—Nguyen Nhac, Nguyen Lu, and Nguyen Hue. According to historical records, Nguyen Hue was the youngest of the three, with Nguyen Nhac as the eldest and Nguyen Lu as the middle brother. Their family origins are traced back to the Ho clan in Huong Cai village, Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An province. The family originally bore the surname Ho, descended from Ho Quy Ly, and followed Lord Nguyen to settle in the South when he crossed the Thay Wall in 1655. Over time, the family changed their surname to Nguyen, following the mother's lineage, due to their marriage to a wealthy merchant's daughter, Nguyen Thi.

Nguyen Hue's father, Ho Phi Phuc, moved the family to Kien Thanh hamlet, where they engaged in the betel trade. This trade led to the family's prosperity and eventual settlement in the region. The family's transition from the Ho to the Nguyen surname marked a significant shift in their social and political status.

## Education and Early Rebellion

Nguyen Hue, along with his brothers, was sent to study both literature and martial arts under the teacher Truong Van Hien. This teacher, a former retainer of Truong Van Hanh, who was the mentor of Nguyen Phuc Luan (Nguyen Anh's father), played a crucial role in shaping the brothers' future. After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh, where he discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel against the existing feudal order.

The prophecy "Tay khoi nghia, Bac thu cong" (Rebel in the West, achieve success in the North) is believed to have originated from Truong Van Hien, marking the beginning of the Tay Son uprising. The brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes, were highly skilled in martial arts and are credited with the creation of several Binh Dinh martial arts styles, including Yen Phi Quyen (Swallow Flight Form), Hung Ke Quyen (Rooster Form), and Doc Lu Thuong (Single Censer Spear).

## Rise to Power and the End of the Trinh–Nguyen Civil War

The Tay Son uprising, led by the three brothers, culminated in the end of the Trinh–Nguyen civil war, which had divided Vietnam for over two centuries. The uprising successfully overthrew both the Trinh in the north and the Nguyen in the south, as well as the Later Le Dynasty. This marked the unification of Vietnam under the Tay Son Dynasty.

Nguyen Hue, the youngest brother, became the second emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated in favor of him. His reign, known as the Quang Trung era, was characterized by a series of progressive reforms and military campaigns.

## Military Campaigns and National Reunification

Quang Trung, as he was known after his coronation, was a brilliant military leader who personally commanded troops from the age of 18. Over 20 years of continuous warfare, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one. His military campaigns were instrumental in the national reunification of Vietnam, as he defeated the invasions of Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north.

## Progressive Reforms and Governance

As emperor, Quang Trung implemented a series of progressive reforms that had a significant impact on Vietnam's development. These reforms included economic, cultural, educational, and military changes. He reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. In education, he improved the examination system, promoted the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions.

Quang Trung also issued an edict seeking talented individuals and heavily utilized many skilled officials such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, and Nguyen Huy Luong. His reforms were highly regarded by historians for their progressive nature, surpassing contemporary Asian countries and helping to bring Vietnam out of the stagnation of the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system.

## Death and Legacy

Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39, marking the end of his reign. His death led to the rapid decline of the Tay Son Dynasty, as his successor, Quang Toan, was too young to lead effectively. The royal court fell into internal conflict, and the dynasty failed to continue resisting the Nguyen Anh forces.

Despite his early death, Quang Trung's legacy endured. He is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of Vietnam's 14 typical national heroes. Many schools and streets in Vietnam are named after him, reflecting his lasting impact on Vietnamese history and culture.

### Role in Taking the Song from Demo to Release

The process of transforming the demo of "Love the Way You Lie" into its final released version involved several key contributors, each playing a distinct role in shaping the song's sound and structure.

#### Mike Strange: Engineer and Mixer
Mike Strange played a central role in the production of "Love the Way You Lie." He recorded and mixed Eminem's vocals at Effigy Studios in Ferndale, Michigan. Strange was responsible for editing the vocals using D-Verb, a reverberation software, and an Extra Long Delay plug-in. He preferred to make minimal changes to the vocals, relying primarily on board compression and console equalization. Strange also used Bricasti and Eventide Reverb 2016 mixing tools to achieve a "brighter" reverberation. His brother, Joe, engineered the track, contributing to the overall production quality.

Strange's approach was to enhance the existing elements of the track rather than overhaul it. He noted that "Everything we needed was already in the track, apart from the vocals." After the initial sessions, Strange worked with Alex da Kid to refine and improve the track, ensuring that it matched and surpassed the demo that da Kid had sent.

#### Alex da Kid: Mixing and Mastering
Alex da Kid was brought in to assist with the mixing and mastering of "Love the Way You Lie." He initially wanted to replace the acoustic guitar on the demo, but Eminem chose to keep it, indicating a preference for the original arrangement. Da Kid's role was to refine the track, ensuring that it met the standards for release. Strange described the process as "simply a matter of trying to match and then to improve on the demo [Alex da Kid] had sent us."

#### Marcos Tovar and Makeba Riddick: Rihanna's Contributions
On Rihanna's side, the recording sessions took place at Sun Studios in Dublin, Ireland, and were engineered by Marcos Tovar. Makeba Riddick, an R&B songwriter, provided additional vocal production, contributing to the final sound of the track. Strange noted that Rihanna was satisfied with her recorded vocals and did not make major changes to her seven stereo vocal tracks, indicating that her performance was already well-crafted and aligned with the song's vision.

### Conclusion
The collaboration between Mike Strange, Alex da Kid, and the engineers and producers involved in Rihanna's sessions was essential in transforming the demo of "Love the Way You Lie" into its final form. Each contributor played a vital role in ensuring that the song was polished, balanced, and ready for release, reflecting the combined efforts of both artists and their production teams.

1,	"Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery (2010). Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production

Rihanna's approval of the song's topic ultimately influenced her decision to work with Eminem.
The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

### **Production and Writing**
The song was written by **Skylar Grey**, who initially created the backing track and hook melody. **Alex da Kid**, a British hip hop producer, contributed to the production by creating the instrumental foundation. Grey's collaboration with Alex da Kid was facilitated by **Jennifer Blakeman**, her Universal Music publisher, who suggested the partnership. Grey also wrote the chorus to the song in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo. **Eminem** later wrote the rapped verses to the song and chose to collaborate with **Rihanna** for the chorus, which he felt only she could perform.

### **Recording**
The recording sessions for the song took place in **Ferndale, Michigan**, and **Dublin, Ireland**. **Mike Strange** was involved in the recording process, though the specific role is not detailed. The track features **acoustic guitar**, **violin**, and **drums**, with **electric guitar** and **piano** used in the chorus. **Alex da Kid** also used various audio processing tools, including **Waves RVerb**, **REQ equalization**, and **MaxxBass plug-in**, to shape the sound.

### **Visual Aspects**
The **music video** for "Love the Way You Lie" was directed by **Joseph Kahn**. The video stars **Dominic Monaghan** and **Megan Fox** as lovers in a violent relationship, with **Eminem** and **Rihanna** appearing in front of a **burning house**. The video's depiction of domestic violence received a mixed reception, with some critics suggesting it was influenced by the real-life abusive relationships of **Eminem** and **Rihanna** with their respective ex-partners, **Kim Scott** and **Chris Brown**.

### **Collaboration and Influence**
The song's themes of domestic violence and abusive relationships were influenced by the personal experiences of both **Eminem** and **Rihanna**. **Rihanna** expressed that the song's theme of domestic violence was impactful because it addressed a topic many people lacked insight into. She also mentioned that she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the song's theme, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table." The song was later followed by a sequel, **"Love the Way You Lie (Part II)",** which was mostly narrated from Rihanna's perspective.

The Hong Bang era, also known as the "Age of the Stone," is a period in Vietnamese history traditionally associated with the rule of the Hung Kings, who are considered the legendary founders of the Vietnamese nation. According to historical and mythological sources, the Hung Kings reigned for a total of **18 generations** during this era. These kings are believed to have ruled from the time of the legendary Hung King Hùng Vương, who is said to have founded the first dynasty, through to the last of the 18 kings, who is often identified as the 18th Hung King, also known as Hùng Vương 18.

The 18 Hung Kings are a central part of Vietnamese folklore and historical tradition, symbolizing the early unification of the Vietnamese people under a single rule. While the exact historical accuracy of these kings is debated by modern historians, they remain a significant part of the cultural and national identity of Vietnam. The reign of these kings is often associated with the establishment of the first centralized state in the region, the development of early Vietnamese civilization, and the consolidation of power over the territory that would later become Vietnam.

Kinh Duong Vuong
[1b] His taboo name was Loc Tuc, a descendant of the Than Nong clan.
Year of Nham Tuat, 17th year. In the past, De Minh, the third-generation descendant of Viem De of the Than Nong clan, fathered De Nghi. Later, during a tour of the South, De Minh reached Ngu Linh, married the daughter of Vu Tien, and fathered the king [Kinh Duong Vuong]. The king was a man of sagacious intelligence; De Minh loved him dearly and wanted him to succeed to the throne. The king persistently yielded to his older brother and dared not obey the command. De Minh then established De Nghi as the heir to rule the North, and enfeoffed the king as Kinh Duong Vuong to rule the South, calling it the kingdom of Xich Quy.
The king married the daughter of Dong Dinh Quan named Than Long, and fathered Lac Long Quan (Note: The Tang annals record: during the Kinh Duong period, there was a goat-herding woman who claimed to be the youngest daughter of Dong Dinh Quan; she married the second son of Kinh Xuyen but was abandoned, and wrote a letter asking Lieu Nghi to report this to Dong Dinh Quan. Thus, Kinh Xuyen and Dong Dinh had been allied by marriage for generations).

Lac Long Quan
[2a] His taboo name was Sung Lam, son of Kinh Duong Vuong.
The king married De Lai's daughter, Au Co, and fathered a hundred sons (legend has it she gave birth to a hundred eggs), who are the ancestors of the Bach Viet. One day, the king said to Au Co: "I am of the dragon race, you are of the fairy race; water and fire are incompatible, it is truly difficult for us to be together." They then bid each other farewell, dividing 50 children to follow their mother to the mountains, and 50 children to follow their father to the South (some versions record to the South Sea), and enfeoffed the eldest son as Hung Vuong to succeed the throne.
Historian Ngo Si Lien said: When heaven and earth were first formed, there was a being created from vital energy, which was the Pan Gu clan. From the manifestation of energy came the manifestation of physical forms; nothing exists outside the two energies of yin and yang. The I Ching says: "Heaven and earth intermingle, all things are transformed and purified; male and female unite their essences, all things are born." Therefore, there is husband and wife first, then father and son, and after father and son comes ruler and subject. [2b] However, the birth of sages and worthies is always extraordinary, which is due to the mandate of heaven. Swallowing a dark bird's egg to give birth to the Shang dynasty, stepping on a giant's footprint to establish the Zhou dynasty, are all recorded facts of this nature. The descendant of the Than Nong clan, De Minh, married the daughter of Vu Tien and fathered Kinh Duong Vuong, who is the founding ancestor of the Bach Viet. The king married the daughter of Than Long and fathered Lac Long Quan; Lac Long Quan married the daughter of De Lai and had the auspicious blessing of fathering a hundred sons. Is that not what laid the foundation for our Viet nation's enterprise? Examining the Tongjian Waiji (Comprehensive Mirror, Outer Annals), it states: De Lai was the son of De Nghi; according to that record, Kinh Duong Vuong was the biological younger brother of De Nghi, yet they intermarried; perhaps it was because that era was still primitive and rites and music had not yet been established?

Hung Vuong
[3a] The son of Lac Long Quan (taboo name unknown), established the capital in Phong Chau (now Bach Hac district).
Upon ascending the throne, Hung Vuong set the national name as Van Lang (this country bordered the South Sea to the east, Ba Thuc to the west, Dong Dinh lake to the north, and Ho Ton - which is Champa, now Quang Nam - to the south). He divided the country into 15 administrative regions: Giao Chi, Chu Dien, Vu Ninh, Phuc Loc, Viet Thuong, Ninh Hai, Duong Tuyen, Luc Hai, Vu Dinh, Hoai Hoan, Cuu Chan, Binh Van, Tan Hung, Cuu Duc; all were vassal lands of Hung Vuong; while the region called Van Lang was where the king established the capital. He appointed civil generals called Lac Hau, and military generals called Lac Tuong. The king's sons were called Quan Lang, and daughters were called Mi Nuong. Officials in charge of affairs were called Bo Chinh; their hereditary succession from father to son was called phu dao. Kings of all generations were called Hung Vuong. At that time, the people living in the forests and mountains saw that the rivers and streams had shrimp and fish, so they invited each other to catch fish for food, but were often harmed by water monsters (thuong luong). The tattooing custom of the Bach Viet people probably started from there.

Ho Phi Tien's wife was Nguyen Thi, the only daughter of a wealthy merchant in Phu Lac, hence they changed their children's surname from Ho to the mother's surname, Nguyen.[9] Their son, Nguyen Phi Phuc, also specialized in the betel trade and prospered. Some documents also suggest that the Ho family changed to the surname of Lord Nguyen as soon as they moved South.[8][9][10] Mr. Nguyen Phi Phuc had 8 children, including 3 sons: Nguyen Nhac, Nguyen Hue, and Nguyen Lu.

Nguyen Hue was born in the year of Quy Dau 1753, the 13th year of the Canh Hung reign under King Le Hien Tong of the Later Le Dynasty. He was also known as Quang Binh,[11] Van Hue[12], or Ho Thom. Later, local people often called him Duc Ong Binh (Lord Binh)[13] or Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight).[8] According to Quang Trung anh hùng dân tộc (Quang Trung the National Hero), "Nguyen Hue had curly hair, textured skin, eyes that flashed like lightning, a voice as resonant as a bell, agile, strong, and brave." The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. 2,	"Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The king married the daughter of Dong Dinh Quan named Than Long, and fathered Lac Long Quan (Note: The Tang annals record: during the Kinh Duong period, there was a goat-herding woman who claimed to be the youngest daughter of Dong Dinh Quan; she married the second son of Kinh Xuyen but was abandoned, and wrote a letter asking Lieu Nghi to report this to Dong Dinh Quan. Thus, Kinh Xuyen and Dong Dinh had been allied by marriage for generations).

Lac Long Quan
[2a] His taboo name was Sung Lam, son of Kinh Duong Vuong.
The king married De Lai's daughter, Au Co, and fathered a hundred sons (legend has it she gave birth to a hundred eggs), who are the ancestors of the Bach Viet. One day, the king said to Au Co: "I am of the dragon race, you are of the fairy race; water and fire are incompatible, it is truly difficult for us to be together." They then bid each other farewell, dividing 50 children to follow their mother to the mountains, and 50 children to follow their father to the South (some versions record to the South Sea), and enfeoffed the eldest son as Hung Vuong to succeed the throne.
Historian Ngo Si Lien said: When heaven and earth were first formed, there was a being created from vital energy, which was the Pan Gu clan. From the manifestation of energy came the manifestation of physical forms; nothing exists outside the two energies of yin and yang. The I Ching says: "Heaven and earth intermingle, all things are transformed and purified; male and female unite their essences, all things are born." Therefore, there is husband and wife first, then father and son, and after father and son comes ruler and subject. [2b] However, the birth of sages and worthies is always extraordinary, which is due to the mandate of heaven. Swallowing a dark bird's egg to give birth to the Shang dynasty, stepping on a giant's footprint to establish the Zhou dynasty, are all recorded facts of this nature. The descendant of the Than Nong clan, De Minh, married the daughter of Vu Tien and fathered Kinh Duong Vuong, who is the founding ancestor of the Bach Viet. The king married the daughter of Than Long and fathered Lac Long Quan; Lac Long Quan married the daughter of De Lai and had the auspicious blessing of fathering a hundred sons. Is that not what laid the foundation for our Viet nation's enterprise? Examining the Tongjian Waiji (Comprehensive Mirror, Outer Annals), it states: De Lai was the son of De Nghi; according to that record, Kinh Duong Vuong was the biological younger brother of De Nghi, yet they intermarried; perhaps it was because that era was still primitive and rites and music had not yet been established?

Hung Vuong
[3a] The son of Lac Long Quan (taboo name unknown), established the capital in Phong Chau (now Bach Hac district).
Upon ascending the throne, Hung Vuong set the national name as Van Lang (this country bordered the South Sea to the east, Ba Thuc to the west, Dong Dinh lake to the north, and Ho Ton - which is Champa, now Quang Nam - to the south). He divided the country into 15 administrative regions: Giao Chi, Chu Dien, Vu Ninh, Phuc Loc, Viet Thuong, Ninh Hai, Duong Tuyen, Luc Hai, Vu Dinh, Hoai Hoan, Cuu Chan, Binh Van, Tan Hung, Cuu Duc; all were vassal lands of Hung Vuong; while the region called Van Lang was where the king established the capital. He appointed civil generals called Lac Hau, and military generals called Lac Tuong. The king's sons were called Quan Lang, and daughters were called Mi Nuong. Officials in charge of affairs were called Bo Chinh; their hereditary succession from father to son was called phu dao. Kings of all generations were called Hung Vuong. At that time, the people living in the forests and mountains saw that the rivers and streams had shrimp and fish, so they invited each other to catch fish for food, but were often harmed by water monsters (thuong luong). [3b] They came to report this to the king. The king said: "The barbarians in the mountains are different from aquatic species; those aquatic species favor their own kind and hate other species, which is why you are harmed by them." The king then told everyone to use ink to tattoo images of water monsters on their bodies. From then on, the water monsters saw them and no longer bit or harmed them. The tattooing custom of the Bach Viet people probably started from there.

The kingdom of Van Lang, established under the rule of the Hung Kings, was a well-structured and organized entity that reflected the political and administrative systems of the time. The kingdom was divided into **15 administrative regions**, each playing a crucial role in the governance and stability of the realm. These regions included notable areas such as **Giao Chi**, **Duong Tuyen**, **Cuu Chan**, **Cuu Duc**, and **Phuc Loc**, among others. Each region was part of the territorial division under the rule of **Hung Vuong**, the founder of the Van Lang kingdom.

The administrative structure of Van Lang was supported by a system of **military and civil officials**. **Lac Tuong** were military generals appointed by Hung Vuong to oversee the defense and administration of the 15 regions. These officials were responsible for maintaining order and ensuring the security of the kingdom. In contrast, **Lac Hau** were civil officials tasked with managing the day-to-day governance of the regions, including the administration of justice and the collection of taxes. This division of responsibilities between military and civil officials ensured a balanced and efficient system of governance.

The **capital of Van Lang** was established in **Phong Chau**, which is now known as Bach Hac district. This location was strategically chosen to serve as the political and administrative center of the kingdom. The capital was also where the king resided and where major decisions were made. The region known as **Van Lang** itself was the heart of the kingdom, symbolizing the central authority of the king.

The **Hung Kings** were not only rulers but also symbolic figures representing the lineage and rule of the Bach Viet people. The title **Hung Vuong** was given to all kings of the Van Lang kingdom, signifying their divine right to rule and their connection to the legendary **Lac Long Quan**, the father of the first Hung King. This lineage was deeply rooted in the mythology and history of the region, reinforcing the legitimacy of the kings' rule.

In addition to the administrative and military structures, the **Hung Kings** also implemented cultural and social practices that shaped the identity of the Van Lang people. One such practice was the **custom of tattooing**, which was introduced to protect the people from water monsters. This practice not only served a practical purpose but also became a symbol of the cultural heritage of the Bach Viet people.

Overall, the organization of the Van Lang kingdom under the Hung Kings was a blend of administrative efficiency, military strength, and cultural tradition. The division into 15 regions, the appointment of military and civil officials, and the establishment of a central capital all contributed to the stability and prosperity of the kingdom during its early years.

### Legends and Customs Attached to the Hung Vuong Era

The document provides several legends and customs associated with the Hung Vuong era, reflecting the cultural and historical significance of this period in Vietnamese history.

#### **Legends of the Hung Vuong Era**

One of the most prominent legends is the story of **King Hung and his daughter Mi Nuong**, who was said to be of divine descent. This legend highlights the mythological and royal lineage of the Hung Kings. According to the narrative, **Thuc Vuong**, a rival king, sought to marry Mi Nuong, but the **Hung Hau** (the king's advisor) warned against it, fearing that it was a ruse to conquer the country. The king then invited two supernatural beings, **Son Tinh (Mountain Spirit)** and **Thuy Tinh (Water Spirit)**, to compete for Mi Nuong's hand in marriage. Son Tinh won the competition by arriving first with lavish gifts, and he married Mi Nuong, living on **Tan Vien mountain**. Thuy Tinh, enraged by his defeat, unleashed floods and aquatic creatures to attack Tan Vien mountain, but Son Tinh successfully defended it with divine powers. This legend illustrates the mythological struggles between natural forces and the divine protection of the royal family.

Another significant legend is the **story of the child prodigy from Phu Dong village**, who, at a young age, demonstrated extraordinary bravery and military skill. This child, who later became a revered figure, was granted a sword and a horse by the king and led the royal army to victory against an enemy. His heroic deeds led to the construction of a temple in his honor, and he was posthumously granted the title **Xung Thien Than Vuong**. This legend emphasizes the theme of divine favor and the emergence of a hero who saves the kingdom.

#### **Customs of the Bach Viet People**

The document also references a **custom of tattooing** practiced by the **Bach Viet people**, which is believed to have originated during the reign of the 6th **Hung King**. According to the legend, the king encountered a problem with **water monsters** that were harming his people. To counter this, the king instructed his subjects to tattoo images of **water monsters** on their bodies. This custom was thought to deter the monsters from attacking, as they would recognize the people as being protected by the images. This practice reflects the cultural and spiritual beliefs of the time, where symbolic markings were used to invoke protection and ward off supernatural threats.

#### **Historical and Political Context**

The document also touches on the **political structure** of the **Hung Vuong era**, noting that **feudal lords** were established to act as a defensive screen for the kingdom. The country was divided into **15 regions**, each governed by a **chief** and **deputy**, with the king assigning his **younger sons** to rule these territories. This system of governance highlights the **centralized yet decentralized** nature of the early Vietnamese state, where royal authority was extended through familial and administrative structures.

In summary, the legends and customs associated with the **Hung Vuong era** reflect a blend of **mythological, cultural, and political elements**, offering insight into the values and beliefs of the time. These stories and practices continue to be an important part of Vietnamese cultural heritage.

[1b] His taboo name was Loc Tuc, a descendant of the Than Nong clan.

Lac Long Quan
[2a] His taboo name was Sung Lam, son of Kinh Duong Vuong.
The king married De Lai's daughter, Au Co, and fathered a hundred sons (legend has it she gave birth to a hundred eggs), who are the ancestors of the Bach Viet. One day, the king said to Au Co: "I am of the dragon race, you are of the fairy race; water and fire are incompatible, it is truly difficult for us to be together." Historian Ngo Si Lien said: When heaven and earth were first formed, there was a being created from vital energy, which was the Pan Gu clan. From the manifestation of energy came the manifestation of physical forms; nothing exists outside the two energies of yin and yang. Therefore, there is husband and wife first, then father and son, and after father and son comes ruler and subject. Swallowing a dark bird's egg to give birth to the Shang dynasty, stepping on a giant's footprint to establish the Zhou dynasty, are all recorded facts of this nature. The descendant of the Than Nong clan, De Minh, married the daughter of Vu Tien and fathered Kinh Duong Vuong, who is the founding ancestor of the Bach Viet. 2,	"Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

According to the books Khâm định Việt sử Thông giám cương mục and Đại Nam thực lục: Nguyen Hue's ancestors were from Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An region. Nguyen Hue was born in the year of Quy Dau 1753, the 13th year of the Canh Hung reign under King Le Hien Tong of the Later Le Dynasty. He was also known as Quang Binh,[11] Van Hue[12], or Ho Thom. Later, local people often called him Duc Ong Binh (Lord Binh)[13] or Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight).[8] According to Quang Trung anh hùng dân tộc (Quang Trung the National Hero), "Nguyen Hue had curly hair, textured skin, eyes that flashed like lightning, a voice as resonant as a bell, agile, strong, and brave." The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. Nguyen Lu was called Duc Ong Bay (Lord Seven) and Nguyen Hue was Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight); Le Trong Ham in the book Minh đô sử argued that Ho Phi Phuc fathered "Nhac, Lu, then two daughters, and then Hue".

Growing up, he, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were sent to study both literature and martial arts with teacher Truong Van Hien. Truong Van Hien was a retainer of Truong Van Hanh, and Truong Van Hanh was the teacher of Nguyen Phuc Luan – Nguyen Anh's father. ### Political and Military Achievements of Quang Trung

Quang Trung, also known as Nguyen Hue, was a pivotal figure in Vietnamese history, renowned for his significant political and military achievements. His leadership during the Tay Son dynasty marked a period of national reunification and reform. Militarily, Quang Trung demonstrated exceptional prowess, leading the Tay Son forces to victory against both the Siamese and the Qing invaders. His strategic acumen and bravery were evident from a young age, as he personally commanded troops starting at the age of 18. Over the course of 20 years, he engaged in numerous battles without suffering a single defeat, showcasing his tactical brilliance and unwavering resolve.

Politically, Quang Trung's contributions were equally profound. He implemented a series of progressive reforms that aimed to modernize and strengthen the nation. These reforms spanned various sectors, including economics, culture, education, and military. In economics, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraging the growth of handicrafts and expanding foreign trade with the West. His efforts to modernize the military included the adoption of advanced weaponry, enhancing the country's defense capabilities.

In terms of education, Quang Trung reformed the examination system to be more practical, promoting a focus on learning and the use of the Vietnamese Nom script over the Han script. He also took measures to eradicate superstitions and streamline religious practices, which contributed to a more secular and progressive society. His policies were highly regarded by historians, who noted their progressive nature and their potential to rejuvenate the nation after a period of stagnation under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system.

Quang Trung's leadership was characterized by a vision that extended beyond immediate military victories. His reforms were designed to create a more equitable and efficient society, reflecting his commitment to the well-being of his people. The impact of his policies was significant, as they not only addressed the immediate challenges of his time but also laid the groundwork for future development. His legacy is remembered not only for his military successes but also for his transformative political initiatives, which continue to be studied and appreciated for their progressive and forward-thinking nature.

He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.
